questions.stem: A retailer records revenue=950 and cost=710 in rupees. Python evaluates profit=revenue-cost; margin=profit/revenue. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: Profit is 240 and margin is approximately 25.26%
Profit is 240 and margin is approximately 33.80%
Profit is 1660 and margin is approximately 174.74%

questions.solution: Profit is 950-710=240. Revenue margin divides profit by revenue: 240/950=0.25263, or 25.26%.

option_explanations.B: This uses cost as the denominator, describing markup.
option_explanations.C: Revenue plus cost is not profit.
option_explanations.D: A currency amount is not itself a percentage.

cards.front: Python calculations: What does this mean?
cards.back: A Python expression computes a value; assignment stores a reference under a variable name. State the unit and business meaning of the result. Example: revenue=900; cost=650; profit=revenue-cost -> profit is 250 in the same monetary unit. Avoid: A numeric result alone does not explain a business decision.

cards.front: List methods: What does this mean?
cards.back: A list is an ordered, mutable sequence. append adds one object; extend adds each item from an iterable. Example: a=[10]; a.append([20,30]) -> a is [10,[20,30]]. Avoid: Appending a list creates one nested item rather than two numeric entries.

cards.front: Loops and conditions: What does this mean?
cards.back: A for loop visits each item; an if condition determines which statements run. Indentation defines the block. Example: amounts=[80,120,150] -> total is 270. Avoid: Count qualifying rows and sum qualifying amounts answer different questions.

cards.front: pandas grouping: What does this mean?
cards.back: groupby splits rows by a key; selecting a numeric column and summing or averaging answers a specific question for each group. Example: West sales: 10,20; East sales: 8 -> West total 30; East total 8. Avoid: A grouped average is not a grouped total; choose the measure from the business question.

cases.title: Store sales aggregation audit
cases.context: A pandas DataFrame contains region and sales columns: (West,10), (West,30), (East,15), (East,missing). The manager wants total observed sales and an honest note about missing entries. Do not assume the missing sales value is zero.

source_references.locator: Independently authored synthetic case; pandas GroupBy documentation

subquestions.prompt: Explain the difference between region sales sum, mean, size and selected-column count; calculate each for West.
subquestions.model_answer: West sum=40; mean=20; size=2; sales count=2. Sum and mean summarize observed amounts, whereas size and count measure rows and nonmissing observations.
subquestions.acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent correct pandas expressions and clearly justified wording earn credit.

subquestions.prompt: For East calculate size and selected sales count. Explain why the difference matters.

rubric.criterion: Explains the one missing sales observation

subquestions.model_answer: East has 2 rows but only 1 observed sales value. The missing amount requires investigation and cannot be assumed to be zero.
subquestions.common_errors: Replacing a missing value by a measured zero without evidence.
subquestions.acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent correct pandas expressions and clearly justified wording earn credit.

subquestions.prompt: Write pandas grouping expressions for observed sales totals and missing-value diagnostics; give the manager a qualified comparison.

rubric.criterion: Correct groupby selected sales sum expression
Uses size and count to expose missing observations

subquestions.model_answer: df.groupby('region')['sales'].sum(); df.groupby('region').size(); df.groupby('region')['sales'].count(). Observed totals are West 40 and East 15, but East has an unobserved sale, so this is not a complete-revenue comparison.
subquestions.common_errors: Claiming complete regional performance from incomplete observed totals.
subquestions.acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent correct pandas expressions and clearly justified wording earn credit.
